note: Values are for the bulk material. 3D-printed parts are weaker and anisotropic; the print knock-down (A2-T2) is applied separately. Entries marked verify=true were taken from the cited datasheet family but not re-read from the PDF in this session; confirm before quoting in the proposal. print_knockdown factors apply to printed parts in the weakest (layer) direction and are deliberately conservative.

PETG.name: PETG copolyester (injection-moulded reference)
PETG.source: Eastman Eastar copolyester 6763 product data sheet (tensile modulus, yield stress, density); Poisson's ratio and conductivity typical for PETG

print_knockdown.source: Conservative worst-direction factors from the FDM anisotropy literature (e.g. Ahn et al., Rapid Prototyping Journal 8(4), 2002: strength across layers is a fraction of in-plane strength); assumes 100% infill

PLA.name: PLA (injection-moulded reference)
PLA.source: NatureWorks Ingeo 4043D technical data sheet (tensile modulus, yield, density); Poisson's ratio and conductivity typical for PLA

print_knockdown.source: Conservative worst-direction factors from the FDM anisotropy literature (e.g. Ahn et al., Rapid Prototyping Journal 8(4), 2002: strength across layers is a fraction of in-plane strength); assumes 100% infill

AL6061T6.name: Aluminium 6061-T6
AL6061T6.source: ASM Aerospace Specification Metals, Aluminum 6061-T6 data sheet
